transcript.content:
<issue>
Layout /tags/list.html panics on edit
See https://discourse.gohugo.io/t/hugo-panic-template-tags-list-html-not-parsed/56971

The following test panics:

```go
// Issue 14740.
func TestEditTagsList(t *testing.T) {
	files := `
-- hugo.toml --
baseURL = "https://example.com"
-- layouts/tags/list.html --
Foo.
`

	b := hugolib.TestRunning(t, files)
	b.AssertFileContent("public/tags/index.html", "Foo.")
	b.EditFileReplaceAll("layouts/tags/list.html", "foo", "Bar").Build()
	b.AssertFileContent("public/tags/index.html", "Bar.")
}
```

OK, so the issue is editing the "legacy mapped" layout names that's also valid in the new setup ...

</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed (Hugo), find code handling "legacy mapped" template names (e.g. tags/list.html mapped to taxonomy/list.html), likely in tpl/tplimpl (legacy mapping, template store, e.g. 'legacyMapped' or 'LegacyMapped'). Report where the template store handles file changes/edit (e.g. a function that reparses templates by name/path, 'not parsed' panic message) and the code that may panic. Show relevant code snippets with file and line numbers.

content.content: {"summary":"Legacy-mapped templates (e.g. tags/list.html mapped to taxonomy/list.html) are handled in tpl/tplimpl/templatestore.go. The \"template %s not parsed\" panic is in templatetransform.go. On a file edit, RefreshFiles re-inserts and re-parses templates. I did not run anything to reproduce a panic. The explanation below comes from reading the code only.","findings":["templatestore.go:265 – TemplInfo has the field `isLegacyMapped bool`.","templatestore.go:211-213 – the options hold the maps legacyMappingTaxonomy, legacyMappingTerm and legacyMappingSection. They are initialised at ~1936-1938 and filled from the layoutLegacyMapping expansion at ~1954.","templatestore.go:1322 insertTemplates(include, partialRebuild) collects the legacy mappings. It builds legacyOrdinalMappings at 1334, converts legacy paths with fromLegacyPath at 1352, and sets applyLegacyMapping at 1383-1389 when the path has at most 2 slashes. It looks up the mapping maps at 1412, 1416 and 1487.","templatestore.go:1552-1580 – for each legacy mapping, insertTemplate2(..., replace=true, isLegacyMapped=true, s.treeMain) is called. The code then sets `ti.isLegacyMapped = true` (1573) and calls s.tns.readTemplateInto(ti), which fills the content but does not parse it.","templatestore.go:1208-1316 insertTemplate2 stores the template with `isLegacyMapped: isLegacyMapped` (1305). At 1310 `if !isLegacyMapped { s.setTemplateByPath(pi.Path(), ti) ... }`, so legacy-mapped templates are not registered by path. Only the treeMain node key is set.","templatestore.go:792 – UnusedTemplates skips templates where vv.isLegacyMapped.","templatestore.go:731-760 RefreshFiles(include) is the edit/rebuild entry point. Its steps are: clearCaches, tns.createPrototypesParse, insertTemplates(include, true), createTemplatesSnapshot, parseTemplates(true), extractInlinePartials(true), transformTemplates, tns.createPrototypes(false), prepareTemplates.","templatestore.go:1630 parseTemplates(replace) skips templates whose state is processingStateTransformed. It calls s.parseTemplate(vv, replace) for the rest. It then finds base templates and applies them, or sets noBaseOf=true and parses again (~1655).","templates.go:48 parseTemplate wraps tns.doParseTemplate. templates.go:72 doParseTemplate returns early with nil, without parsing, when `!ti.noBaseOf || ti.category == CategoryBaseof`. The parse then waits for the base template. Otherwise it parses ti.content into the prototype under the name pi.PathNoLeadingSlash(), with a counter suffix if !replace.","templatetransform.go:72-86 applyTemplateTransformers has the main panic: `tree := getParseTree(t.Template); if tree == nil { panic(fmt.Errorf(\"template %s not parsed\", t)) }` (line 84). This fires when a TemplInfo reaches the transformer without a parsed Template. A legacy-mapped template that is re-inserted on refresh but not parsed, for example one skipped by the early return in doParseTemplate, would trigger it.","templatetransform.go:94-99 getParseTree does an unchecked type assertion, `templ.(*htmltemplate.Template).Tree`. It panics if t.Template is nil or of another type.","Other panics: templatetransform.go:130-154 (panic(err) in the transformer setup), templates.go:60 and 67 (newBlankTemplate), templates.go:293 (\"prototypeHTML not set\"), templates.go:324 (\"unknown template type\"), templatestore.go:430 and 1220 (\"category not set\"), templatestore.go:819 (template func namespace not found)."],"confidence":0.7}

content.content: {"summary":"readTemplateInto is in templates.go:19-40. It reads the template file, strips any leading BOM, and sets noBaseOf from needsBaseTemplate unless it is already true. noBaseOf is set in the places listed below.","findings":["templates.go:19-40, full body: `func (t *templateNamespace) readTemplateInto(templ *TemplInfo) error { if err := func() error { meta := templ.Fi.Meta(); f, err := meta.Open(); if err != nil {return err}; defer f.Close(); b, err := io.ReadAll(f); if err != nil {return err}; templ.content = removeLeadingBOM(string(b)); if !templ.noBaseOf { templ.noBaseOf = !needsBaseTemplate(templ.content) }; return nil }(); err != nil { return err }; return nil }`. Line 31 sets content. Lines 32-34 set noBaseOf.","templates.go:189: noBaseOf: true in a TemplInfo struct literal. The literal copies D and matrix from `overlay`.","templatestore.go:241: field declaration `noBaseOf bool`. The comment at 243 says that if it is false, the final template is looked up in the base template tree.","templatestore.go:1024: ti.noBaseOf = true for inline templates (SubCategoryInline).","templatestore.go:1103: ti.noBaseOf = true for embedded templates. The comment says none of them need a baseof.","templatestore.go:1174: noBaseOf: true in a struct literal with category CategoryShortcode.","templatestore.go:1304: noBaseOf: category > CategoryLayout, in the TemplInfo constructor.","templatestore.go:1657: vv.noBaseOf = true when FindAllBaseTemplateCandidates returns none. content.content: {"summary":"Reproduced the panic in the second build. Two TemplInfos are both named 'tags/list.html' in the second build (/tags 'list' and its legacy-mapped 'taxonomy' twin). Both are parsed with replace=true into the same shared html/template namespace, so they collide. The panic was on the non-legacy 'list' entry, whose Template is non-nil but whose parse Tree is nil. The debug prints and the test file are removed and git status is clean. The mechanism is partly inferred: I did not read the html/template internals to confirm why the Tree ends up nil.","findings":["Build 1 (initial, replace=false): both /tags entries are inserted with Template==nil and state=0. The non-legacy one is nk{1 list html} (ti=0xc0001fc280, name tags/list.html, noBaseOf=true, isLegacyMapped=false, CategoryLayout). The legacy one is nk{1 taxonomy html} (ti=0xc0001fc500, noBaseOf=true, isLegacyMapped=true). After parsing, the first keeps the name 'tags/list.html' and the legacy one is renamed 'tags/list.html-1'. This is because doParseTemplate (tpl/tplimpl/templates.go ~L70-90) appends '-N' to the name when !replace and the name already exists in the prototype. Neither is yet transformed after parse (state=0). After transformTemplates all of them reach state=1.","Build 2 (RefreshFiles, replace=true), before parseTemplates: both /tags entries are new objects with Template==nil, state=0. The 'list' entry is ti=0xc0004e6640 (name tags/list.html, noBaseOf=true, legacy=false, CategoryLayout). The 'taxonomy' entry is ti=0xc0004e6780 (name tags/list.html, noBaseOf=true, legacy=true).","Build 2, after parseTemplates: both have tmplNil=false and state=0. The 'taxonomy' entry is still named 'tags/list.html', with no '-1' suffix this time. The whole /tags group of tags/list.html entries is the only non-baseof set that was rebuilt, and the earlier-parsed entries from build 1 stay at state=1.","Build 2 panic: transformTemplates then calls applyTemplateTransformers (tplimpl/templatetransform.go:84) and panics with 'template /tags/list.html not parsed'. getParseTree(t.Template) returns nil for the non-legacy 'list' entry (the trace shows the 0xc0007fe500-style non-legacy ti, i.e. the one parsed first). My extra debug print guarded on Template==nil did not fire, so the Template is non-nil and only its Tree is nil.","Why: doParseTemplate skips the unique '-N' renaming when replace=true, so prototype.New('tags/list.html').Parse(content) runs twice with the same name, once for the real layout and once for its legacy-mapped duplicate (taxonomy -> tags/list.html). The second Parse replaces the first entry in the shared template set, so the first *Template no longer has a valid Tree. In the first build, replace=false gave the legacy twin a unique name 'tags/list.html-1', so this did not happen.","Likely fix direction: under replace, give legacy-mapped duplicates a unique name, or skip/re-point them, or have the transform step look the template up by name instead of holding the stale handle."],"confidence":0.7}
